correctness.rationale: An independent sign decomposition gives the powered-distance spectrum. Orthogonality gives distance two between different indices on the same bipartite side, distance four between antipodes, and distance three for opposite-side nonedges. On the sign-even subspace A₂ acts as 2(J_k−I_k) separately on the two sides, A₃=A₁ and A₄=I. On the sign-odd subspace A₂=0, A₃=−A₁, A₄=−I; the off-diagonal block of A₁ is H with all singular values sqrt(k). This yields the stated eigenvalues and multiplicities on the zero-sum subspace. On [0,1], G is strictly increasing, and F for k≥8 is strictly concave with F(0)=−1, F(1)=0 and F′(1)<0, yielding the claimed first crossings. The zero sector excludes p>1. At k=4 and p=1 only the +sqrt(k) sector is negative; below 1 the bipartition eigenvalue is the fourth forward difference of x^p at zero and is strictly negative by the positive integral representation of x^p as a mixture of 1−exp(−tx). Centered Gram ranks give all endpoint dimensions. Independent rational bounds confirm the switch at k=8 and 12, and high-precision bisection confirms the reported decimals. Substituting p=x/k or x/sqrt(k) in the first-root equations and bracketing by strict limiting signs yields the respective asymptotics. The strict statement at p=0 uses the usual convention D₀=J−I.
residual_risks: The replay confirms finite scalar comparisons, not the all-order theorem; its proof uses the universal sign decomposition and analytic inequalities. Claims are conditional on existence of a Hadamard matrix of the given order.
